text:
anya: heads-up — seeing metadata growth in kv-cache on small hosts. staging repro: after ~48h the per-prefix metadata map hits ~2.1GB and OOMs the shard. looks like tombstone accumulation + lease snapshot churn. cc @keiko @jared

jared: can you paste a sample of the metadata shape?

anya: here's a sanitized example from the dump:
```json
{"prefix":"/p/abc","last_access_ms":1700000000000,"leases":[{"id":123,"claim_ts":1700000010000}],"tombstones":[{"key":"k1","deleted_ts":1700000020000}],"compacted":false,"pinned":false}
```

keiko: we intentionally avoided aggressive compaction because of lease correctness complexity. but this growth is real — we should evaluate incremental compaction that never blocks the fast path. :thinking:

marco: quick tradeoffs: compact-on-evict keeps steady-state small but spikes eviction latency. background-scanner keeps eviction cheap but adds IO and complexity for correctness across leases and handoffs.

jared: another option: lazy compaction on read-touch. when a prefix is accessed, stream-compact metadata under a tight cpu/io budget. avoids background IO for cold clusters.

anya: ran quick benchmarks — lazy-on-read reduced overall metadata size but added ~12% p99 on the hot read path in the microbench. a background job with per-shard rate limiting reclaimed ~70% of metadata in 30m and kept p99 stable.

keiko: interface boundary question — who should own compaction? runtime or lease-manager? my vote: runtime owns mechanics, but expose opt-out hooks so Dedicated/private deployments can control policy.

infra-bot: canary: compaction-candidate flag enabled on stg-eviction-02 at 2024-11-11T15:23:00Z

marco: correctness note — compaction must preserve tombstones until all relevant leases have advanced past the delete. propose adding a versioned compaction id so we never regress visibility during handoff.

jared: sketch for implementation: add `compaction_id` (monotonic int) to prefix metadata and `compaction_checkpoint` to leases. Compaction marks entries compacted with id=N and retains per-lease deltas for any lease with checkpoint < N. GC only when all checkpoints >= N.

keiko: + metrics required: `compaction_reclaimed_bytes`, `compaction_duration_ms`, `compaction_backpressure_count`, and `compaction_inflight_per_shard`. Also a config knob for budget: ms/sec and bytes/sec.

anya: tentative rollout plan:
1) PoC background compaction job with shard budget = 50ms/s and 1MB/s IO cap.
2) add `compaction_id` + `compaction_checkpoint` fields (backwards compatible).
3) 48h soak on staging with full workload.
4) canary 10% prod if stable.
I'll open an RFC and include benchmarks, failure modes, and migration steps.

marco: :thumbsup: include a lazy upgrade migration (no big GC pass). Also add a kill-switch to disable compaction quickly if we misbehave.

anya: noted. any other concerns?

jared: please enumerate failure modes in RFC: compaction job crash mid-run, partial compaction with checkpoint mismatch, and handoff race where compaction_id advanced but target shard hasn't applied deltas.

keiko: and add tests: cross-shard handoff with compaction in-flight, read-after-compact correctness, and long-running lease hold while compaction runs.

anya: will add all that to the RFC and ping this thread when it's up. thanks everyone.
